result.description: SaaS ecommerce platform (hosted storefronts, catalog, orders, checkout, customers) with REST and GraphQL APIs.
result.auth_detail: Store-level API account: merchant creates client ID/secret + static access token (sent as X-Auth-Token). App-level: modified OAuth2 auth-code grant, per-store access token. Account-level tokens also exist. Storefront GraphQL uses JWT bearer tokens.
result.access_detail: Gate 1: store-level API accounts are created by each merchant themselves (no review), but a multi-tenant OAuth toolkit where other merchants click-install needs app-level OAuth, and the docs say only an app approved for public availability can generate tokens on behalf of other store owners; Marketplace submission has a $99 review fee and needs a Partner ID assigned after approval. Gate 2: dev needs a store to test; free 15-day trial and partner sandbox exist, but end merchants need a paid BigCommerce plan after trial to keep an active store. So not purely self-serve. Per-merchant self-created API tokens would be self-serve, but OAuth app flow for others requires approval.
result.api_notes: Large REST surface (V2/V3: catalog, orders, customers, carts, checkout, payments, promotions, shipping, webhooks, themes, scripts) plus GraphQL Storefront and Admin GraphQL. Base https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{hash}.
result.blocker: Public multi-merchant OAuth requires Marketplace app approval ($99 fee, Partner ID); otherwise users paste store hash + store-level token. Official MCP is docs-only, not store operations; store-ops MCPs are community.

evidence.quote: BigCommerce offers three types of OAuth-based API accounts to developers who wish to use BigCommerce’s REST APIs: store-level credentials, app-level credentials, and account-level credentials.
However, when an app is approved to be publicly available for additional stores to install, it can generate access_token s on behalf of store owners and authorized users.
A payment window opens for the $99 review and listing fee.
Merchants generate single-store API credentials when they create API accounts in their store control panel, in the Settings > Store-level API accounts menu.
Complete REST and GraphQL API docs.
Connect Cursor, Claude, or Codex to the BigCommerce developer docs via MCP.
